title: openai-compat: tool_choice semantics, schema mapping, and tool message formatting fixes
author: Zoe Kim
release_notes: Fixes and clarifications to OpenAI compatibility layer: correct tool_choice semantics, ensure schema->function mapping correctness, preserve tool-origin message formatting during streaming; no API breaking changes.
body: Motivation: the openai-compat layer must faithfully implement tool/function calling semantics used by OpenAI-style models. We observed three related issues in production: (1) tool_choice responses from some model variants were being interpreted as assistant messages instead of explicit tool selections, (2) schema->function mapping did not handle optional/nullable properties consistently which caused validation and runtime panics in edge cases, and (3) streaming path for tool outputs lost original message formatting (role/metadata) causing downstream consumers to misattribute content. This PR fixes the above by: implementing strict tool_choice detection and canonicalization, enhancing schema mapping to support nullable/optional fields and array-of-object coercions, and preserving tool-origin message framing in the streaming path. Changes are backwards-compatible for existing API consumers but correct previously-observed misbehaviors.
commits: feat(openai-compat): implement canonical tool_choice handling and semantics
fix(openai-compat): preserve tool-origin message formatting during streaming
fix(schema-mapper): handle nullable and optional properties consistently (arrays/objects)
test(openai-compat): add unit/integration tests for tool_choice and schema mapping
docs(openai-compat): update compatibility notes and examples for tool calling
chore: bump compatibility test fixtures and golden files
review_comments: Elena Ruiz (reviewer): Please add a unit test for tool_choice when model returns both 'tool' call and an assistant message in the same response chunk. Was this observed in the canary?

Author (Zoe): Added a fixture and unit test that simulates interleaved chunks; behavior is now deterministic and documented in the test. Also added a comment in tool_choice.go explaining canonicalization rules.

Markus Nguyen (reviewer): The schema_mapper change looks good but please ensure we don't silently drop unknown properties when mapping to a function signature. Could we add a debug-level metric for dropped fields?

Author (Zoe): We now surface dropped/extra fields via a debug metric (openai_compat.schema_extra_fields) and log them at debug level; these are included only when debug is enabled to avoid noise in prod metrics.
Samir Patel (approver): Verified end-to-end with the streaming canary and the SDK interop test. Approving after minor nits addressed (doc wording and a missing linter directive).
ci_checks: e2e-canary: flaky initially (1 failing stream test) -> rerun -> passed
notes_on_rollout: Canary deployed to 10% of traffic for 48 hours. No errors above baseline were observed; schema-mapper debug metrics emitted in canary region flagged a small set of deprecated tool payloads from an internal model version which were whitelisted and backward-normalized. After 48h canary we rolled to 100%.
post_merge_tasks: Add migration note to internal ops runbook about tool_choice enforcement
Coordinate with models team to update generator fixtures for deprecated tool payloads
Backport minimal fixes to release/2026-02 for a hotfix if customer incidents surface
notes: This PR consolidates several small fixes and tests. No change to public API signatures; SDK contracts updated to reflect corrected behavior (SDKs were already tolerant).
